-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 1 - HIGH LEVEL
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3.4 is a copy of 3.2 (Build Settings index 5, after 3.3). The only difference in the scene is four
check boxes on MainPlayer's CubeRailRunner (Input section), all ON in 3.4 and OFF (default) everywhere else:

  sideWallRunnerRule        Fix A  one side-wall rule, no timing
  keepSpinOnSideWall        Fix B  never overwrite a direction already used on the leg
  settleRederiveClearFaces  Fix C  after a 0.2 s pause, re-read left/right from the screen
  useDrawnViewForMapping    Fix D  decide against the camera as it is drawn, not where it is going

The Legacy feel is kept: left/right are still decided by the first press on a leg, then held while you keep
pressing; on top/bottom faces LEFT is still the face drawn on the left of the screen; double tap still = roll
+ 90 degree flip to the face opposite where you started.

What a press does in 3.4, in plain words
  * On TOP / BOTTOM (or any face where the two choices are clearly left and right on screen): LEFT = the face
    drawn on the left, RIGHT = the face drawn on the right (unchanged from 3.2).
  * On a LEFT / RIGHT side wall of a flat leg (both choices drawn straight above/below the runner):
    RIGHT = the runner's own clockwise roll (seen from behind), LEFT = counter-clockwise - from the moment of
    landing, whenever you tap. (3.2: a different rule for the first 0.2 s, then this one.)
  * Keep pressing (gaps shorter than 0.2 s after a roll ends): the cube keeps turning the same way round.
  * Stop for 0.2 s with nothing queued or rolling, on a face where the screen is clear: the next press is read
    from the screen again (LEFT = face drawn left). On a side wall the spin direction you used is kept.
  * During a camera swing the screen you see is used, not the end of the swing. If at that instant the two
    choices are drawn on top of each other (the swing passes the angle where they swap sides), the end-of-
    swing view decides.


-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 2 - THE ALGORITHM IN 3.4  (PlayerController.cs, class CubeRailRunner)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Unchanged: input paths (keys / touch / SimulateTap -> EnqueueTap), double tap (0.22 s, same leg, same key),
FlipToOpposite, queue, cooldowns (0.08 / 0.03 / 0.10), fair corners, nextLegBuffer, UpdateLegView (legView
still = settled view at landing; used by everything that is not the mapping).

Decision (DecideLegSign, called by DotProductRollDir when the leg's sign is 0 and a press is PLAYED):
  view    = useDrawnViewForMapping ? drawn camera rotation (CameraParentRotator.boomCamera) : legView
  dest    = AngleAxis(-90, heading) * faceNormal(face)          // where raw +1 lands
  screenX = dest . view.right
  |screenX| > 0.15                     -> SCREEN-X: RIGHT = sign(screenX)                     (as 3.2)
  else, sideWallRunnerRule on:
     face is LEFT/RIGHT                -> SIDE-WALL: RIGHT = +1 (clockwise seen from behind)    (Fix A)
     TOP/BOTTOM stacked (only possible
     mid-swing under the drawn view)   -> screen-x under legView (end of swing) if clear       (Fix D fallback)
     still stacked                     -> +1 and a warning "[RollMap] HEADING rule reached" (counter HeadingRuleHits)
  else (3.1-3.3)                       -> HEADING rule (as before)
Looks (TapDirectionToReach, PredictSide, SideAfterRoll, corner grace, PeekPressFace) never decide the sign in
3.4: they answer what a press would do now. PredictSide simulates the first queued press deciding the sign
from the face it is played on and later ones keeping it. (3.2 unchanged: a look still locks the sign.)

UpdateSideFaceRemap (3.2's 0.2 s side-wall rule, still on):
  keepSpinOnSideWall: returns without touching the sign if a press has been played on this leg or the sign is
  already set (Fix B). Leaving the side wall keeps the sign (3.2 cleared it to 0).

UpdateSettleRederive (new, every FixedUpdate, Fix C):
  settleTimer counts real seconds (shrunk by timeScale, like the old remap) on the current face while nothing
  is queued, rolling or buffered; reset by any new press (Enqueue) and by any face change.
  timer >= flipRemapDelay (0.2 s) and sign != 0 and |screenX| > 0.15 on this face (with the mapping view)
     -> sign = 0, the next press re-decides with SCREEN-X. (LastRemapChangeTime is set only when that changes
        what LEFT/RIGHT mean.) Stacked side walls are skipped - their held sign stays.
  Checked every step, so a camera swing that ends while the runner is settled re-derives too (Fix D).

Which rule is in charge, by situation (all seen in the recordings):
  first press, clear face        SCREEN-X, drawn camera
  first press, flat side wall    SIDE-WALL (+1), from landing
  more presses < 0.2 s apart     HELD (keeps spinning)
  after a 0.2 s pause            clear face: SCREEN-X again;  stacked side wall: HELD
  mid-swing, choices stacked     end-of-swing view (ScreenXSettledView)
  HEADING rule                   never (0 hits in every 3.4 run)


-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 3 - DOUBLE TAP AND FLIP  (unchanged)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Same key twice within 0.22 s on the same leg = flip to the face opposite the one before the first tap. The
first tap is played on the next physics step, so in practice it is a 90 degree roll then a 90 degree flip,
turning the same way. Recorded in 3.4: 56 double taps over all 10 passes, every one ended on the right face.
Swipe up/down = one 180 degree flip.


-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 4 - FINDINGS 1-4, BEFORE (3.2) AND AFTER (3.4)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
All numbers: same seeded paths in both scenes, bot pressing real screen taps (see PART 5).

FINDING 1 - on a side wall the same press changed meaning after 0.2 s                       -> FIXED (A)
  Before: legs 2, 11, 14, 27 (seed 3) are the "disagree" side walls (RIGHT face heading screen-left, LEFT
  face heading screen-right): at landing the HEADING rule said one thing, 0.2 s later the remap the other.
  Leg 11 (heading -Z, camera behind, landed LEFT, needs BOTTOM):
      3.2  react 0.05 s: the bot had to press RIGHT -> BOTTOM;  react 0.35 s: LEFT -> BOTTOM.
           With 0.35 s the press did NOT do what LEFT/RIGHT meant at landing (1 of 25 first presses).
      3.4  react 0.05 s: LEFT -> BOTTOM;  react 0.35 s: LEFT -> BOTTOM.
  After: at landing leg 2 RIGHT -> BOTTOM (like old legs 17/19), legs 11/14/27 RIGHT -> TOP (like old legs
  24/27), and that is what every press did. The agreeing side walls (legs 3, 8, 15-19, 22, 28 - the class of
  old legs 2, 5, 6, 13, 16, 18, 20, 23, 30) are unchanged. HEADING rule reached: 0 in every 3.4 run.
  LEFT/RIGHT at landing, react 0.05 vs react 0.35: identical on all 30 legs, in both scenes.
  (The old recording's leg numbers can't be replayed - it was not seeded - so the same leg classes are shown.)

FINDING 2 - the remap overrode a direction the player had already used                      -> FIXED (B)
  Repro (your example): on TOP/BOTTOM press X -> side wall, wait 0.5 s on the wall, press X again: it must go
  on round to the face opposite the start. "keep-spin probes", seeds 3/1/5/7:
      3.2  16 probes, 7 FAILED (bounced back to the start face)
      3.4  16 probes, 0 failed

FINDING 3 - the held sign ignored the screen once the runner had gone round the cube            -> FIXED (C)
  Over-roll pass: one extra roll past the needed face, pause 0.3 s, then correct like a player would - press
  the side of the screen where the needed face is drawn (or, if it is drawn straight above/below, press the
  other key to undo). Seeds 3/1/5/7:
      3.2  46 corrections, 21 WRONG  (by screen side 13 of 26 wrong, undo-when-stacked 8 of 20 wrong)
      3.4  45 corrections,  0 wrong
  This covers both repros: faces of vertical legs (e.g. leg 3 type: wait 0.3 s, RIGHT goes to the face drawn
  right) and BOTTOM after a flip. Fast presses still spin: in the over-roll pass the extra roll comes 0.25 s
  after the first press (before 0.2 s of quiet after the roll) and always carried on round (0 mismatches).
  Settle re-derives in 3.4: about 15-28 per 30 legs, of which 8-21 actually changed what LEFT/RIGHT meant.

FINDING 4 - the mapping used the end of a camera swing, not the screen                          -> FIXED (D)
  Seed 3 has two swings: 225 -> 135 (landing leg 6) and 135 -> 45 (legs 23-24).
  Leg  6 (vertical, landed BOTTOM): drawn 205, settled 135. 3.2 mapped at 135, 3.4 at 205/187 (drawn).
         Both: LEFT -> LEFT face, which is drawn on the left in both views - same result here.
  Leg 23 (vertical): the swing to 45 starts during the leg. 3.2 kept 135; 3.4 used 133 (drawn). Same result.
  Leg 24 (flat, heading -Z, landed BOTTOM, needs TOP = double tap), landed at drawn 103, settled 45:
      3.2  at landing LEFT -> RIGHT face, RIGHT -> LEFT face  (answer for yaw 45 - opposite to what is drawn
           at yaw 103, where the runner's RIGHT face is drawn on the right)
      3.4  at landing LEFT -> LEFT face, RIGHT -> RIGHT face  (what is drawn)
           press at +0.06 s (drawn 100): RIGHT -> RIGHT face (drawn right)
           press at +0.36 s (drawn 82):  the two faces are drawn almost on top of each other (|x| <= 0.15), so
           the end-of-swing view decided: RIGHT -> LEFT face (which is where it ends up drawn right).
      This is the ONLY place where a 3.4 press did something other than what LEFT/RIGHT meant at landing
      (1 of 25 first presses at react 0.35; also seen on leg 24 of seeds 7 and 3 in the probe passes). It is
      the swing passing through the angle where the two faces swap screen sides; the double tap still reached
      TOP every time. If you would rather freeze the landing answer until a swing finishes, that is a one-line
      change - say so.

Scripted runs, every pass, 3.4: 0 deaths, 0 press/face mismatches (the face each press reached was always the
face PeekPressFace said just before it), 0 HEADING rule hits, 0 outside taps.
Same for every clean 3.2 pass: 0 deaths, 0 mismatches. One 3.2 pass (keep-spin seed 5,
first try) had 13 taps that did not come from the bot - keyboard input reaching the Game view - and was
re-run; the logger now flags such taps.

HumanSimPlayer soak (Average model, seed 777, 300 s of game time each, run n laid from seed 777+n in both
scenes, runs stopped at score 49 per the under-50 test rule):
      3.2  9 runs, mean 22.1, median 22, 2 reached the cap   (7, 49, 49, 3, 27, 12, 6, 22, 24)
      3.4  7 runs, mean 29.1, median 27, 1 reached the cap   (38, 49, 48, 5, 27, 26, 11)
  Same path for the same run number: 3.4 scored the same or better on 6 of the 7 shared paths. Small sample -
  read it as "no worse", not as proof. NOTE: the sim taps through TapDirectionToReach, i.e. it always knows the
  mapping; it cannot show screen confusion. The bot passes above do that.
  The first soak attempt scored ~1 in BOTH scenes: HumanSimPlayer had a live-mode bug - it set nextLookAt
  ("look again once the roll has played") but never read it, so at editor frame rates it planned a second
  press before its first had played and then fired it off the needed face. Fixed in HumanSimPlayer.Think (one
  line, test tool only).


-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 5 - HOW IT WAS TESTED / SAFETY CHECK / HOW TO READ
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  * Same path every run: DynamicPathGenerator.SeedRuns(seed) (new, tooling only, never called by the game)
    gives the layout its own seeded stream (all of the generator's Random.Range calls and the portal runway
    shuffle now go through PathRange - unchanged behaviour while unseeded) plus seeded boost/bridge/decoy/
    obstacle/wave streams. Verified: all 30 legs identical across passes in both scenes (landing face
    included). Seed 3 was picked from a scan of seeds 1-8 because it is the one with two camera swings in the
    first 30 legs (seed 4242, used first, never turned the camera).
  * Power diamonds turned off for each test session (play mode only) - the autopilot rolls by itself.
  * Bot = Assets/Scripts/LeftRightDebugTxt.cs, pressing through CubeRailRunner.SimulateTap (the key/touch path).
    It picks its taps with CubeRailRunner.PeekPressFace (new, read-only; the game's own mapping, both scenes).
      react:0.05 / react:0.35   first tap that long after landing (and between its own taps)
      overroll                  one-roll legs with >= 0.95 s left: press, same key 0.25 s later (extra roll),
                                pause 0.3 s, correct by the screen side the needed face is drawn on (or the
                                other key if it is drawn straight above/below)
      keepspin                  TOP/BOTTOM -> side wall on flat legs with >= 1.25 s left, and two-roll legs:
                                press, wait 0.5 s, same key again; expected = face opposite the start
    Double taps alternate a 0.04 s and a 0.10 s gap.
  * Soak = Assets/Scripts/LeftRightSoak.cs (HumanSimPlayer, cap 49). Both tools are dev-only, never in a scene.
  * Scene safety (modification-time marker taken before any change, plus SHA-256):
      files newer than the marker: MainScene prop camera 3.4.unity (saved once, at creation, 18:21),
      ProjectSettings/EditorBuildSettings.asset, and scripts. 3.1 / 3.2 / 3.3 .unity and the difficulty
      profile: byte-identical to before (mtimes 15:21 / 16:35 / 17:05, before this work).
      Code: every new path is behind one of the four toggles (default false); with all four off, DecideLegSign
      is the old maths line for line, looks keep their old side effect, and the settle step returns at once.
      3.3's ScreenProjected path is not touched (PredictSide's new branch is skipped when projected).
      3.2's recordings with the new code show the old behaviour (HEADING at landing on side walls, the 0.2 s
      remap, 0 settle re-derives).
  * Frame lines: as in the 3.2 file, plus "yaw drawn/settled/mapping", [spot] is where the target face is
    drawn relative to the face the runner is on, rule = held / side-remap(held) / would-decide:<rule>
    (ScreenX, SideWall, ScreenXSettledView, Heading). Leg blocks list every press: time after landing, kind,
    key, from -> result, what the bot expected, what LEFT/RIGHT meant at landing, yaws, rule.
